metadata.title: Claude, Applying Brand Guidelines.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude branding a document is general design taste or something more specific, using the applying-brand-guidelines skill's own description as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that a brand-guidelines skill is SKILL.md, a spec Claude reads, applies, and validates the same way against whatever document you hand it.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (hand the skill a slide deck: same three steps run every time; then the same pipeline runs identically twice, and just as readily against a document outside the scope)

beats.narration_text: Someone wonders how you'd get Claude to match your brand. But matching a vibe isn't it — this skill applies a written spec. So: how does that work?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'How do I get Claude to match our brand?', hesitates on 'match', corrects to 'apply', lands the real question

props.text:
How do I get Claude
to match our brand?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('match' -> 'apply') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works — not something it's trained on. This one is applying-brand-guidelines: apply_brand.py, validate_brand.py, REFERENCE.md, and a four-kilobyte SKILL.md holding the full instruction set, plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads the file, then acts. The file is the program.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder opening to four files, SKILL.md highlighted; 'not trained on it' callout; 'the file is the program' closer

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon opens into four file rows: apply_brand.py (14k), validate_brand.py (10k), REFERENCE.md (3k), and SKILL.md (4k) — SKILL.md recolors teal and grows slightly. A 'not trained on it' tag crosses out a brain glyph. Closing line: 'the file is the program'.

beats.narration_text: The instructions sit in a Steps section: read SKILL.md, execute each step in order, return the result — linear, no branching unless a step says so. Watch the anchor. Hand the skill a slide deck: it reads the deck, applies your colors and fonts, and hands back a branded deck. Same three steps, every time.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — three linear pipeline phases, then a slide deck arrowing through apply_brand.py to a branded-deck output

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — a slide deck, three steps
production_viz.mechanic: Three phase cards appear left to right and connect with arrows: 'read SKILL.md' / 'execute' / 'return result'. They fade back. THE ANCHOR. A card labelled 'slide deck' arrows into a card labelled 'apply_brand.py', which arrows into a card labelled 'branded deck'. Closing line beneath: 'same three steps, every time'. THIS EXACT SEQUENCE RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Same input, same output, every run — hand it the identical deck twice and apply_brand.py returns the identical branding both times. That's the payoff of a file being the program. But the reverse holds too: hand it a document outside the stated scope — external communications only — and it still runs the same steps, against material the SKILL.md never specified. validate_brand.py is the check: wrong colors, wrong fonts, wrong scope, all caught the same way.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same pipeline firing identically twice, then split: identical deck twice = identical branding; document outside scope = same steps still run, both checked by validate_brand.py

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same input, same output; then the limit
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 PIPELINE RETURNS, identical, running twice in a row — two matching 'branded deck' cards appear side by side, labelled 'same input, same output'. Then it splits: left card 'in-scope document' → pipeline → clean branding, labelled 'the payoff'; right card 'out-of-scope document' → the same pipeline → branding applied anyway, labelled 'the limit'. Beneath both, a small 'validate_brand.py' tag with a check and a cross — wrong colors, wrong fonts, wrong scope. Closing line: 'only what SKILL.md names'.

beats.narration_text: Applying brand guidelines isn't Claude developing its own sense of style — it's SKILL.md, a spec Claude reads, applies, and validates the same way against whatever document you hand it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I want to apply brand guidelines to my team's documents. Read the applying-brand-guidelines skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. Watch for that walk-through — explaining first is what surfaces which steps SKILL.md actually specifies, and where the scope stops. Liam, in for Bear.
